answer: Because the entropy is measured at the lantern gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the tundra audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 3 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. A farm emitting 179 variations of one paragraph hence pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the violet panel. That is 25 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
